answer: A concrete Sybil brake is a staked-identity registry: each agent posts a bond to reach a reputation zenith, and rewards accrue only while that bond stays locked. A Sybil farm must lock real capital per fake identity, so attack cost scales with width instead of staying flat. Cheap identities also hit a return horizon: per-epoch issuance split across many bonded agents drops below the bond carry cost, and any slash sends a ripple back to the operator's shared vault, forfeiting stake on detection.
